resolvedFindings.origin: verification static challenge, reproduced and fixed by architecture
resolvedFindings.before: An invalid first URL could leave queued completion state, then a later inquiry using the same elicitationId could become associated with that old completion.

red.observed: Expected no inquiry for a retired ID, observed one.

resolvedFindings.after: First connection dispatch retires every well-shaped URL ID before later validity checks. Reuse is rejected. QueuedGuard removes queued entries on every create exit; cancelling prompt dispatch discards its queued prefix.
resolvedFindings.green: Included in the final 14-test protocol output.

resolvedFindings.before: An unknown request with a valid parent returned an error without preserving its original details for that owner.

red.observed: Expected one unavailable event, observed zero.

resolvedFindings.after: Only a live parent matched by exact serialized requestId on this connection receives the original method/params unavailable event. The response remains method_not_found; no executable action or responder is registered.
resolvedFindings.green: Included in final 14-test protocol output; exact method_not_found code is confirmed statically, while this fixture asserts the failed parent and retained raw details.

reviewedInvariants: Synchronous send and parent request registration share a short mutex interval; the receive lookup shares that mutex. RequestGuard removes parent ownership and expires only entries matching that connection and parent.

OpeningGuard enables session/load reverse questions before load responds. Its cleanup checks the exact Operation abandonment Arc, so an older opening cannot remove a newer owner for the same native ID.
Both completion lookup and queued-prefix extraction take pending before queued. create retains pending until insertion; completion cannot pass through a missing-owner interval.
A completion before consent expires the obsolete protocol responder without constructing accept. Complete never resolves authenticate or another parent request; parent errors remain errors.

URL accept omits form content and keeps the temporary lease until completion or parent end. Form content uses the existing response shape. Decline/cancel/late answer do not manufacture external completion.

Operation abandonment, reverse-request cancellation, prompt cancellation and exact connection cleanup remove applicable pending entries. Late completion after cancellation has no live entry to mutate.

Pending URL state is in memory, connection-local, bounded by 32 pending entries and 4096 retired URL IDs. Accepted URLs require https with a host, no credentials, control characters, whitespace framing or backslash. No backend URL opening/fetch was introduced.
Existing DebugTap reconstructs a fixed content-free record; reviewed inquiry code has no database or log write of URLs, form values or raw request content.

excludedHypotheses.hypothesis: Normal prompt/config requests must be registered under requestId too.
excludedHypotheses.result: Not a supported defect: the official v1 page defines requestId for interactions outside a session; normal session traffic uses sessionId. This does not prove every other outside-session method is implemented.

priorAssociatedRegressions.qualification: Read original prior logs; not re-run by this reviewer and not substituted for integration tests after final changes.

limits: Only authenticate/session new/load currently register request-scoped parent ownership. Initialize and other outside-session operations are not proven or universally supported; unowned inquiries reject instead of being assigned to the current UI.
Only advertised form and URL modes are supported; unknown modes or extension methods are not executable. External URL handling is https-only in this increment.
No real Agent, login/provider, remote authorization, installed UI, Windows or all-Agent acceptance was exercised by this review.
This receipt does not independently endorse the frontend, user consent/opening flow, or full application integration; those have separate reviews/tests.
The protocol fixtures execute the real manager/stdio path with synthetic peers. Their outcomes are not evidence that a real third-party endpoint completes successfully.
